summary:
SOMA — Um mapa do corpo para a missão
Menos números soltos. Mais contexto para cuidar da tripulação.
Em missões espaciais longas, compreender o próprio estado de saúde não devia exigir que cada astronauta interpretasse tabelas clínicas. O SOMA organiza os indicadores por sistemas corporais e reúne, num só painel, o que foi medido, o que tem registos e qual é o próximo passo informativo — para que a tripulação e a equipa médica possam começar pela mesma visão.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
SOMA is a living map of the astronaut’s body. A clickable human figure is divided into physiological systems (brain and eyes, balance, heart and circulation, lungs, bones, muscles, immune system, metabolism and sleep), following NASA’s human research risks. Each region changes color (green, yellow, red) according to the astronaut’s own baseline. Clicking a system shows what it does in plain language, why spaceflight affects it, the astronaut’s trend, what to do now, and when to call for help. The astronaut logs measurements (blood pressure, heart rate, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood), and SOMA turns them into trend charts and a clear status. Synthetic data generated through an API is used for demonstration.

What benefits does it offer?
Astronauts understand their own health without being doctors. Scattered numbers become an integrated, simple and actionable view, with clear escalation criteria. The flight surgeon can receive a summarized view.

What is the intended impact?
Better-informed, more autonomous health self-assessment on long missions, where help from Earth is delayed. SOMA aims to support, never replace, medical care.

What tools did you use?
Python, pandas and NumPy for data handling and the baseline and trend calculations. The prototype is a Progressive Web App (PWA). AI assistance (a large language model) was used to help with the development, and this will be disclosed in the submission.

What is the creative aspect?
Instead of dashboards full of numbers, SOMA is a body you can touch: a living map that explains, personalizes and recommends actions, designed for the astronaut first and for the ground second.

What factors did your team consider?
We designed SOMA to be always ready. As a PWA, it is meant to keep working even when the connection window is unstable. We also considered responsible use: SOMA is an informational prototype, uses demo data, and makes no diagnostic or clinical claims.
